brief.scope: Fresh recheck after test corrections. Verify only the accepted P2/three-P3 dispositions from the original review against corrected task-output tests and supplied ruling/fix receipt. Confirm load_outputs valid/invalid JSON discrimination, no keyword fallback, extensible transport defaults, real renamed-job rendering, preservation and frozen public seams. Reproduce relevant tests or explicitly rely on receipts if execution is unavailable. No implementation/source/test edits or expanded audit. Inline REVIEW <=1000 words with actual model/ref, approve/changes and exact remaining findings; approve tests for independent implementation only if complete.

envelope.note:
REVIEW — model claude-opus-5 (Opus 5), ref 026fcad433aab03d802e98063b5d9a4a67e759ba against 710dbac38c3b187eb4b3302308430c0a6dec4d76. Verdict: approve (0 p1, 0 p2, 0 p3, 1 opinion). Scope held: the four accepted dispositions, preservation, frozen seams. No repository file was read-modified; the only file I wrote is the control module under this dispatch's out/.

Execution: this profile runs Python 3.12.3, so the receipts were re-measured, not relied on. `python3 -m unittest discover -s ops/devlane/task/tests -p 'test_job_outputs*.py'`: Ran 99, FAILED (failures=95), 0 errors, 0 collection failures. Per file: test_job_outputs.py 60/60, test_job_outputs_accept.py 21/17, test_job_outputs_render.py 18/18 — the fix record's split exactly. `-p 'test_*.py'`: Ran 312, failures=95, 0 errors; 312−99=213 existing task tests, all green, and the 95 failures account for themselves file by file, so nothing outside the new suite is red. The four remaining greens are the three HistoricalRecordsRemainValid tests and test_without_the_flag_an_inlined_plan_is_still_refused — all kwargs-free calls to today's envelope.validate, green because they pin preservation, not because a seam was skipped. sha256 of outputs_support.py, the three test files and duplicate-path-member.json match the record's frozen hashes at 3e91abe byte for byte, so the reviewed tree is the fixer's output.

P2, load_outputs discrimination — corrected and verified by planted faults. LoadOutputsJsonText (test_job_outputs.py:426-490) now carries two positive arms and five refusals, and validate_outputs stays native-data. I ran three faulty counterparties against the class (out/control_faulty_counterparty.py, `python3 -m unittest discover -s <out> -p 'control_*.py'`, 3 tests OK): (A) blanket "refuse any str" — the exact no-op the original P2 named — now fails test_well_formed_json_array_text_loads_to_the_native_list and test_empty_json_array_text_loads_to_omission; (B) json.loads plus a competent native validator with no repeated-member detection fails exactly one test, test_duplicate_json_object_members_are_refused, and nothing else; (C) the same decoder with an object_pairs_hook that rejects repeated keys passes all seven. The fixture is one line, `[{"kind":"file","path":"A.md","artifact":"a","path":"B.md"}]`, whose parse is otherwise a valid single-row array, so the only way to refuse it is to see the duplicate member before dict collapse. That is a real discrimination, not a vacuous one, and the contract row is now pinned on a declared text seam instead of an invented polymorphism.

P3 fallback — corrected. outputs_support.validate_envelope (lines 85-106) raises AssertionError naming the keywords instead of rewriting the call onto validate(env); the accept tests that exercise a seam call require_outputs_param()/require_inline_param() first. Measured effect: the accept file went 8 green to 4, and the four that were green incidentally (the three inline-narrowness tests plus test_omission_does_not_require_declared_file_keys) now fail on one legible line — `AssertionError: 'outputs' not found in mappingproxy(OrderedDict({'env': <Parameter "env">})) : missing public seam envelope.validate(..., outputs=, out_root=); found signature (env)`. A parameter named differently now produces that message, not a scatter. A `**kwargs` catch-all would not satisfy assertIn on the signature either.

P3 transport defaults — corrected. test_job_outputs.py:496-503 asserts issuperset({COMMIT_MSG, last-message.json}) and assertNotIn("tmp"), so an adapter leaf may join the default without forcing the implementer to edit a frozen test, while the two required leaves and the scratch exclusion stay pinned.

P3 renamed rendering — corrected. test_job_outputs_render.py:92-116 now builds two specs differing only in name, plants both the difference and the sameness, drives both through outputs_from_job, and renders each. If outputs_from_job leaked job identity into the array the equality fails, so the case has detection power it did not have; it remains partly redundant with test_job_outputs.py:207, which is what the ruling asked for.

Preservation. The diff against 710dbac is 10 files, all `new file mode`, zero removed lines: no pre-existing test is edited, relaxed or deleted, and no implementation, contract, catalogue or settings file is touched. The intra-branch arithmetic reconciles exactly: 94 tests − 2 moved + 7 new = 99; 86 failures − 2 moved + 7 new + 4 de-incidentalized = 95. Nothing was dropped to buy the corrections.

Frozen seams. The set an independent implementer must match, unchanged apart from the one addition the ruling ordered: OUTPUTS_SCHEMA, TRANSPORT_RESERVED, validate_outputs(value, reserved=), load_outputs(text, reserved=), outputs_from_job(spec), render_declared_outputs(outputs, out_root), append_declared_outputs(prompt, outputs, out_root), validate(env, outputs=, out_root=, inline_planning_exception=), with OutputsError optional and falling back to EnvelopeError. HANDLE_MAX is existing and resolves. Reds are assertions throughout; a missing name never errors collection.

Opinion, not a finding. With the string case moved to load_outputs, no test now requires validate_outputs to refuse a bare str — test_a_non_array_declaration_is_refused covers a dict only. The ruling put that duty on the text seam deliberately and no contract row is left unpinned, so this is not chargeable; if a later pass wants belt and braces, one assertRaises on validate_outputs("[]") would close it without touching anything else.

Freeze readiness: yes. The four accepted dispositions are all present, discriminating and measured at this ref, existing tests are intact, and the suite is ready to freeze for an implementer who must not be the author or the fixer of these tests.
